title: Phased Exposure Builder with Spectator View and Surge Quarantine
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Design a phased exposure builder that lets operators create staged traffic exposures with a read-only 'Spectator' view for stakeholders and a quarantined surge lane for emergency isolation. The goal is to make rollouts easier to reason about at-a-glance while providing fast, reversible controls for incidents and a clear audit trail for compliance. This ticket covers the interaction flows, low-fidelity prototype, accessibility checks, and handoff notes for engineering and product review.
acceptance_criteria: A visual composer exists for creating staged exposures (phases) with percentage sliders and duration controls
Spectator view presents a compact, read-only timeline and live metrics overlay without exposing control buttons
Surge Quarantine lane can be attached to a rollout to divert a configurable percent of traffic for investigation and auto-eviction rules
Emergency rollback is discoverable within two clicks from the active rollout canvas and displays estimated impact before confirm
Prototype demonstrates integration points for telemetry (latency, errors, token-cost) and toggles for canary vs A/B splits
Design includes content for onboarding tooltip and a short microcopy glossary explaining phases, quarantine, and spectator semantics
All mockups pass basic color-contrast checks and keyboard navigation for primary composer controls
decisions: Use a horizontal timeline canvas (phases as cards) instead of nested lists to better surface sequencing and overlap
Represent traffic allocation primarily with draggable sliders and allow numeric entry as a secondary action
Spectator view is a read-only rendering of the same canvas with an overlay showing live signals; controls hidden behind a 'request control' affordance
Surge Quarantine implemented as a first-class lane that can be added to any stage; quarantine has auto-evict rules that are configured in a secondary modal
Emergency rollback triggers a safety modal that shows estimated traffic movement and linked runbook before confirmation
design_notes: Key trade-offs: sliders provide fast mental model for percentage but can hide small-value adjustments; resolved by secondary numeric input and snap-to-safe-values. Prioritize visible safety signals (red/amber/green) and provide inline links to related runbooks. Performance note: timeline should be virtualized for large numbers of phases. Provide an authoring help drawer that surfaces recommended phase templates (canary-short, ramp-24h, a/b-50-50).
